branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Unilateral Ocular Mass with Ulcerated Surface and Anaplastic Cells

excluded_candidates: Benign ocular tumor: reason ranked lower due to anaplastic cells and high proliferative index
Infectious process: reason ranked lower due to absence of infectious symptoms and presence of anaplastic cells
root.label: Subacute Unilateral Ocular Mass with Ulcerated Surface and Anaplastic Cells
supporting_facts: Amelanotic, pedunculated mass with ulcerated surface
Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells

static_evidence_items.content: Chief complaint: 4-week history of rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
Ocular examination findings: normal except for an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
No evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
Histopathology: 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Microscopic Examination: solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Immunohistochemistry: positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
Immunohistochemistry: Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings: negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies: no tumor
Figure A: Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Figure B: Proteinaceous material on the ulcerated tumor surface (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×25)
Figure C: Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×400)
Figure D: Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×100)
Figure E: Nuclear staining for Ki-67 reveals a high proliferative index (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×50)
